text:
Jen (support): hey team — just got a high-priority escalation from AcmeCorp: customers hitting intermittent 429s and some high tail latency when they burst. customer says they see normal traffic then a sudden "burst" for ~30s and then errors. ticket attached: https://support.internal/acme/7890
Mike T.: pinging eng-sre. do we have a repro for their traffic shape? any recent rate-limit changes?
Jen (support): not from them yet — they gave traces + sample client patterns. looks like repeated short requests, small payloads, ~500rps for 20s, then drops. their app retries aggressively which might worsen it.
Ana K.: can you paste the trace snippet? also which env — hosted-prod or dedicated?
Jen (support): hosted-prod. trace snippet: "request_id=abcd status=429 route=/v1/generate latency=120ms" repeated. they have bursts from mobile clients (many devices).
Mike T.: ok. this smells like our per-route token-bucket + burst window hitting the backend concurrency limit. we need a reproducible loadtest that mimics many short-lived clients. I'll propose a plan: 1) small requests (64-128 tokens), 2) 400 rps sustained, 3) 20-40s bursts to 2k rps, 4) client-side retry policy same as their SDK (3x with jitter).
Oliver P.: also capture per-request latency and the 95/99/99.9. throw in some cold-starts for warm pools.
Sam R.: I'll spin up a lab harness. using k6 + our internal loader. sample k6 script:```js
import http from 'k6/http';
import { sleep } from 'k6';
export default function () {
  http.post('https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate', JSON.stringify({prompt: 'hi'}), {headers: {Authorization: 'Bearer x'}});
  sleep(Math.random() * 0.15);
}
```
Jess L.: include a token-bucket shim to apply per-client RPM to mimic mobile-device aggregation. otherwise load generator looks too smooth.
sre-bot: note: run tests in staging first. tag results with `burst-cal-2026-03`.
Mike T.: hypothesis: our default per-API-KEY rate limiter uses a 60s window with burst allowance = 3x baseline. for many small connections retries + connection churn can cause short-term exceeding of backend worker capacity. need to validate whether burst window or global concurrency is the limiter.
Ana K.: I'll instrument the runtime to log token-bucket state + queue lengths. enable debug flags:```yaml
runtime:
  token_bucket:
    window_seconds: 60
    burst_multiplier: 3
  max_concurrency_per_model: 512
  queue_threshold_ms: 200
```
Sam R.: running initial staging run now — will spin up 1k virtual clients, shape: 400rps -> ramp to 2k for 30s -> back to 400 -> repeat 3 cycles. capturing 1s resolution metrics.
(10m later)
Sam R.: first run results: at ramp -> 2k we see 5-7% 429s, 99p latency spikes to 1.2s, queue length jumps and many token_bucket.dropped events. attaching log excerpt:```
[2026-03-15T14:12:03Z] token_bucket: key=acct:acme tokens=0 allow=0 drop=1
[2026-03-15T14:12:05Z] queue: model=redwood-13B queue_ms=850
```
Mike T.: that's consistent. two failure modes: (A) token-bucket denies -> 429, (B) queueing hits queue_threshold -> backend rejects or times out -> 503/504 depending.
Jen (support): customer saw 429s only, not 503s. they also blamed SDK retry behavior.
Jess L.: try variant with client-side retries disabled to see if retries are amplifying the burst.
Sam R.: rerun without retries: 429s drop to ~1%, 99p latency still spikes but fewer drops. suggests retries amplify the denial rate.
Ana K.: interestingly, when we extended window_seconds from 60 -> 120 and reduced burst_multiplier from 3 -> 2, we got fewer 429s during the same burst shape and queueing reduced. tradeoff is lower short-term flexibility but smoother behavior.
Oliver P.: can we compute a recommended default per-API-key RPM/TPM and burst config for hosted self-serve? propose baseline: RPM=1200, TPM=20000, burst_multiplier=2, window=120s, burst_recovery_ms=30000. these are conservative but reduce customer-visible 429s for mobile bursts.
Mike T.: we should tie defaults to observed traffic patterns by plan tier. free tier = stricter (RPM=600, burst_mult=1.5). pro = baseline above. enterprise = configurable/reservations.
Jen (support): for AcmeCorp, would changing retry policy on SDK help immediately? yes, recommend exponential backoff with capped retries and jitter. I'll send them a patch and guidance.
Sam R.: added more runs with different model concurrency knobs. raising max_concurrency_per_model from 512 -> 768 reduced queue_ms spikes but increased per-node memory pressure. not ideal global change.
Jess L.: suggestion: implement short-lived soft-429s with Retry-After header to guide SDKs rather than hard 429s. or provide a 429 with a small cooldown token that allows N requests in next Xs.
Ana K.: added a metric dashboard: https://grafana.internal/d/burst-cal/2026-03-burst-cal showing token bucket fill, queue length, 95/99 latency across runs.
Mike T.: action items: 1) Sam to run full matrix (window=60/120, burst_mult=1.5/2/3, RPM baseline 600/1200/2400) and upload csv. 2) Ana to add token_bucket debug logs behind flag. 3) Jess to prototype soft-429 header. 4) Jen to communicate interim SDK retry guidance to AcmeCorp and update support playbook.
Sam R.: started matrix now, ETA 6h. I'll post the CSV and short summary.
(6h later)
Sam R.: matrix done. key takeaway: window=120 & burst_mult=2 yields lowest customer-visible 429s across most realistic mobile shapes. CSV: https://artifacts.internal/burst-cal-1934567890.csv
Mike T.: ok let's codify defaults for hosted self-serve and staging rollout: apply to new API keys immediately, and gradual rollout for existing keys with opt-out. target rollout next week.
Jen (support): thanks — I'll update the support KB and email AcmeCorp steps. also logging this for a postmortem/template in /product/incidents.
Oliver P.: small note — watch cost impact: longer windows mean higher sustained allowance; add guardrails to prevent abuse (rate-limiting score, anomaly detection).
Jess L.: I'll open an RFC for soft-429 with header semantics and include SDK changes.
sre-bot: scheduled: rollout-window=2026-03-22T02:00Z, canary=1% -> 10% -> 100% over 48h.
Jen (support): closing the escalation for now, will reopen if AcmeCorp reports reoccurrence after SDK changes. :thumbsup:
Mike T.: thanks everyone. great collaboration.
(emoji reactions and short +1s throughout)
